Bill.BriefDescription: Creating a pilot program for the collection of payroll records on public works projects.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to creating a pilot program for the collection ofpayroll records on public works projects; and adding a new section tochapter 39.12 RCW.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 39.12 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The legislature finds that the current process for collectionand disclosure of certified payroll records on public works projects isan inefficient use of public resources and results in unreasonabledelays for interested parties seeking the records. The legislaturetherefore intends to create a pilot program for the collection ofpayroll records on public works projects. (2) The department of labor and industries must contract out for alabor compliance software program that allows contractors andsubcontractors on public works projects to electronically submitcomplete and current payroll records to awarding agencies. At aminimum, the labor compliance software program must collect informationnecessary to ensure compliance with prevailing wage requirements,including names and identifying information of workers, daily hours p. 1 SB 5823worked per pay period, the prevailing wage classification applicable tothe worker, and the wages earned by the worker in the pay period. Thedepartment of labor and industries may consult with the department ofenterprise services and with the capital projects advisory review boardwhen selecting the labor compliance software program. (3) The awarding agency for any public works project subject tothis section must require the contractor and each and everysubcontractor on the project to submit current and complete payrollinformation using the labor compliance software program before anypayment or disbursement of public funds. Following the finalacceptance of a public works project, funds retained pursuant to RCW60.28.011 may not be released to the contractor until the awardingagency has complete and accurate payroll records for every contractorand subcontractor who performed work on the project. (4) Participation in the pilot program is mandatory for publicworks projects advertised for bid on or after January 1, 2014, andbefore January 1, 2019, as follows: (a) For fouryear institutions of higher education, public worksprojects estimated to cost one million dollars or more; (b) For public school districts, public works projects estimated tocost one million dollars or more; (c) For King county, public works projects estimated to cost onemillion dollars or more. (5) Participation in the pilot program is optional for all otherpublic works projects. An awarding agency may participate in the pilotprogram on a projectbyproject basis, and must disclose pilot programparticipation in the bid solicitation.
